title: Neutron-star kinetic heating by TeV inelastic dark matter: does the LZ-fit cross-section light up old neutron stars?
question: For the corpus inelastic fits (Higgsino 7.4e-39, dark photon 1e-42-2e-39, P021 sigma_n(delta)), is capture in a neutron star geometric, what kinetic-heating temperature and near-IR flux result, what would a 2000 K old NS imply, and can white dwarfs and the Sun capture delta=300-380 keV DM?
headline_result: All LZ-fit cross-sections exceed the NS geometric threshold sigma_crit=2.5e-45 cm^2 (3.6e-44 proton-only) by 30-3e7, so an old isolated 1.5 Msun/12 km NS is heated to T_inf=1609 K (2389 K with annihilation) at rho=0.4 GeV/cm^3 independently of the model, delta being 0.2% of the 243 MeV available; WDs also scatter it (delta_max 2-7 MeV) but heat only to 50 K; the Sun captures it only on core Fe/Ni, where the Higgsino annihilates at (1-7)e22 s^-1, 1e2-1e3 above the IceCube scale
